human_actions_pending.context: Unchanged and still the top item, now with a legal edge: privacy 3(2) and 3(4) describe the on-leave wipe and the Clear-Site-Data purge, and the published policy text is ahead of production. The live site has neither leaveWipe nor /explain-that-inchi/__leave. Image builds clean and was smoke-tested locally in the previous session.

human_actions_pending.action: Curl __leave through the upstream proxy after deploying
human_actions_pending.context: The proxy's HTTP Basic gate may 401 the beacon. A 401 carries no Clear-Site-Data header, so the purge silently does nothing and privacy 3(4) is false in production. Still the only link in the chain never tested outside a local container. Command: curl -sI -u eti -X POST https://cheminfo.beilstein.org/explain-that-inchi/__leave | grep -iE '^(HTTP|clear-site-data)'

human_actions_pending.context: The workflow is gone (df4121d) but the gh-pages branch still exists on origin and GitHub still serves it, so a stale copy of the app is live with no __leave endpoint and now with legal pages that no longer match what it ships. Disable Pages in Settings -> Pages, then: git push origin --delete gh-pages. Outward-facing, left for the operator.

human_actions_pending.action: Decide the Clear-Site-Data origin blast radius
human_actions_pending.context: Now disclosed rather than resolved: privacy 3(4) states the purge works per origin and covers everything on cheminfo.beilstein.org. That makes the policy honest but does not make the behaviour desirable — it is safe only if no other application on that host stores browser state. No path-scoped variant exists; the fixes are a dedicated subdomain or dropping the purge.

human_actions_pending.action: Confirm log rotation is <= 14 days on the host
human_actions_pending.context: Privacy 2(2) promises log deletion within 2 weeks. nginx.conf defines no access_log directive, so retention is a logrotate concern on the server. Unbacked claim, carried across three sessions now.

decisions.decision: coi-serviceworker is declared in both attribution surfaces rather than removed
decisions.rationale: It is inert under nginx (returns early because COOP/COEP arrive from the origin) but is kept deliberately as the fallback for any host that cannot set headers — see the previous session's decision. Something shipped in dist/ has to be attributable, and since it is vendored rather than installed, package-lock.json could never cover it. Licence compliance already held: the distributed file carries its MIT notice on its own first line.

decisions.decision: Privacy 3(4) discloses the origin scope instead of the purge being narrowed
decisions.rationale: Clear-Site-Data is scoped by spec to the origin; there is no path-scoped variant, so the only ways to narrow it are a dedicated subdomain or no purge at all. Both are infrastructure decisions for the operator. Disclosure was the change available in text, and it is the one that makes the document true today.
Nothing in the recent changes touches operator identity, board members, foundation number or disclaimer.

decisions.decision: Left the Terms sentence 'The complete dependency list with resolved versions is in package-lock.json' as-is
decisions.rationale: coi-serviceworker is not an npm dependency, so the sentence stays true in its own terms, and the new entry carries the version inline. Rewriting the framing to hedge one vendored file would cost more clarity than it buys.

next_action: Rebuild and redeploy the container (docker compose up --build), then curl __leave through the proxy to confirm the Basic-auth gate is not swallowing the Clear-Site-Data header. Nothing in the repo is pending.
